name: Question 19
problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,3)$, $P(3,-1,4)$ and $Q(-1,0,1).$
worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,3⟩,\,p=⟨3,-1,4⟩,$ and $q=⟨-1,0,1⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-1,4⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-4i+2j+6k \\  & =⟨-4,2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =⟨3,-1,4⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z-10 & =0 \\ 4x-2y-6z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points A(1,−2,3), P(3,−1,4) and Q(−1,0,1).

a
4x−2y+6z+21=0
b
4x−6y−2z+17=0
c
2x−4y−6z+13=0
d
4x−6y−2z+7=0
e
4x−2y−6z+10=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points A,P and Q are a=⟨1,−2,3⟩,p=⟨3,−1,4⟩, and q=⟨−1,0,1⟩.

First, using the 3 points we build 2 vectors parallel to the plane:

v1=AP→=⟨3,−1,4⟩−⟨1,−2,3⟩=⟨2,1,1⟩v2=AQ→=⟨−1,0,1⟩−⟨1,−2,3⟩=⟨−2,2,−2⟩

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[211]×[−22−2]=ijk211−22−2=−4i+2j+6k=⟨−4,2,6⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=⟨3,−1,4⟩⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩r⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=10

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=10−4x+2y+6z=10−4x+2y+6z−10=04x−2y−6z+10=0.
